image_prompt: Dawn-blue night photo of the Chicago skyline seen from Lake Michigan, with the Willis Tower and the Loop towers small and low on the right third of the frame, sitting near the bottom; behind them a nuclear fireball and mushroom cloud, moderately sized, glows bright orange and yellow, lighting the clouds, the glass towers and the water. The whole left half and the upper area are empty dark blue sky.

Orbital view looking down at an angle on Lake Michigan and the American Midwest at dusk, with glowing city lights: the lake on the right side of the frame, Chicago at its southern tip where a gigantic, extremely bright orange and yellow nuclear fireball and mushroom cloud fills about 40 percent of the frame, lighting up the clouds and the coast with a wide orange glow. Exactly one bright orange missile trail arcs in from the upper right down to Chicago. Curved horizon with a thick bright light-blue atmosphere glow, the horizon and sky light and luminous blue. The left side is light blue clouds and sky.

Night photo of a huge ballistic missile bursting up out of the ocean surface from a submerged submarine, with an enormous blinding orange and white rocket flame, towering white spray and glowing smoke lighting the waves; the missile climbs diagonally to the upper right. Stormy ocean, deep blue night sky, no ship visible, the left side empty sky.
